- An operation naming a handshake the specification does not declare, a handshake whose establishedBy names no operation or an operation that itself travels in an envelope, and an upload stream that names a handshake are each reported as handshake in both builds, with the same words.
- An upload stream on a method other than post or put, or whose request body is not one media type of a binary string, a download stream whose success response is not one such media type, and a maxResponseBytes beside no download are each reported as stream in both builds, with the same words.
- Every operation that names a handshake derives the red case expired handshake <name>, which names the lifetime's end and, when the handshake declares uses, the envelopes it has carried.
- extract go writes a dxlib endpoint registered with an end-to-end-encryption type as an operation under a handshake of dxlib's pre-key exchange, asking which operation establishes it, an upload or download stream type as a stream, and asks at a type it does not read.
- generate openapi with the dxlib dialect writes the endpoint type each operation's handshake and stream give; generate go-dxlib writes the exchange's handler, the hooks that seal and open the envelope, the helpers that stream a body in and out, and a client that performs the handshake, the encrypted call and both streams; a generated client calls a generated server over the encrypted API and streams a file larger than its buffers both ways.
- The technical specification lists each handshake with what a client does and marks each operation that travels in one or streams a file, in place of a request body and JSON responses.

**Insight:** A service whose operations travel in an encrypted envelope, or that streams large files, could not say so in its specification, so a client built from it would send plain JSON to an endpoint that expects an envelope, and a document would show a field table where a stream of bytes travels.

### SA-78

specarch generate ui shall write, through specarch-gen-ui-swiftui, the task, list and form pages and the views of a specification for the iPhone in SwiftUI, from an implementation file in Swift whose ui target is platform iphone, so that the screens follow the design's fields, checks, refusals, events and permissions as the Next.js and Carbon screens do, drawn by the components the ui-components idiom names for swiftui.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- generate looks up specarch-gen-<target>-<framework> for an implementation file whose target names a framework, or a platform with a default one, before specarch-gen-<target>-<language> and specarch-gen-<target>, and falls back in that order when one is not on PATH.
- Each page becomes a schema file under Sources/<module>/Pages that holds data only, one Swift literal typed by the part's schema type, with the idiom's names as its labels, and a view file that hands the schema to the part's component behind the guard with the routes its events lead to; the components that read the schemas are written once under Sources/<module>/Screens on SwiftUI alone, the routes once as one enum the app's navigation stack follows, every text once in Strings.swift in the target's language and in each translation the settings name, and the theme as Theme.swift through the design-tokens idiom.
- A task page, a list, a form and a view take the same design keywords, settings, hooks, checks as rules in the data, refusals and events, and report the same errors, as the TypeScript generator does, but for the server routes, which an app does not have, and the comparison of a schema built by hand, which is TypeScript's.
- Each list, form and view that needs a permission gets a derived test under Tests/<module>Tests that it is refused to someone signed in without it, sends someone signed out to sign in and opens to someone who holds it, and the menu a test that no entry shows without the permission of the page it opens, in Swift Testing.
- Under info.wireNames snake_case the schemas name the fields, the session's properties and the paginated-list idiom's names on the wire as the TypeScript generator's do, and a parameter's own name and a route's parameters are not mapped.
- The library lending example's generated package builds with swift build and passes swift test on a Mac, and generated over its sign-in and second-factor screens written by hand it differs only by the header.

**Insight:** The iPhone is the platform the owner's own apps are built for, and a screen written by hand there drifts from the design as one on the web does; the roadmap names SwiftUI the default for the iPhone, and the same pages drawn twice from one specification are the check that the design, not a stack, holds the screens.

### SA-82

A specification shall be able to declare the caller, one record of who is making the call with properties typed as fields, and on a role the rows it reaches in an entity, one expression over the entity's fields and the caller's properties written caller.<property>; specarch validate shall check both in both builds and reserve the name caller in a file on meta-model 0.3, reading a 0.2 file with a warning, the derived cases shall cover what a caller sees outside their rows, generate sql shall write each rule as a row security policy where the engine has one, and the technical specification shall show the caller and the rows each role reaches.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1, NEED-2, NEED-3.

Acceptance criteria:

- A rows rule keyed by a name that is not an entity, one that does not give true or false, and one naming what is neither the entity's field nor the caller's property are each reported as rows in both builds, with the same words.
- A dot outside caller.<property>, a property the caller does not declare, and the caller named in a check constraint are each reported as caller_property in both builds, with the same words.
- A field, a schema's or a view's property or an algorithm's input named caller is reported as reserved_name in a file that says 0.3, and the same file that says 0.2 is read with one meta_model_version warning and no error.
- For every role with a rule and every operation over the entity whose permission the role holds, specarch derive writes the case of the list showing only the rows, of a read by key outside them answering not found, and of a change that would leave them being refused; a job acting as the role gets the case of acting on those rows only.
- generate sql writes the rule as a row security policy on PostgreSQL, with the caller's properties read as the implementation file maps them and an unset or empty one read as NULL, gives every role with no rule on that table a policy holding for every row, and marks the role's rule on an engine with no row security without dropping it.
- The technical specification lists the caller's properties and, beside the permissions matrix, the rows each role reaches.
- generate go-dxlib warns at every operation over an entity with a rows rule, written or derived from the tenant scope, of a role that holds the operation's permission, and at every job acting as the role on the entity, naming the role and the rule, wherever the generated code does not apply the rule.
- generate go-dxlib applies every rows rule over an entity in the list, the read by key and the create, as a condition over the roles and properties of a Caller the service supplies; a caller sees and creates only the rows of the roles they hold, a record outside them is not found and a create outside them is refused with no row stored; the round trip shows it for two tenants on PostgreSQL.

**Insight:** A member sees only their own loans, and a tenant's staff only their organisation's records, and the meta-model could say neither, so the rule lived in prose beside the role and the service enforced what no test derived and no policy carried.

### SA-83

A specification shall be able to declare its machine clients, each by its software_id with its kind, the versions it is admitted at, the roles it holds and how it proves its identity on each request; to say on an operation or command the explicit subset of who may call it, people and clients by name; to close a route on purpose with the reserved permission nobody; and to narrow a role's grant to the clients it holds through; specarch validate shall check each in both builds, the derived cases shall cover every refusal, and the technical specification shall show the clients beside the roles, the callers of each route and the grants narrowed by client.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1, NEED-2, NEED-3.

Acceptance criteria:

- A client whose kind is neither application nor service, one with roles and no proof, a service with no proof, one naming an undeclared role, one whose version range does not parse, and one whose version has no claim to be checked against are each refused in both builds, with the same words.
- A signed request naming an algorithm RFC 9421 does not register or covering a component that is not a request part is refused as proof in both builds.
- A callers list that is empty, names what is neither people nor a client, lists a client twice, lists a service with no roles, or lists a client none of whose roles grants the permission is refused as callers in both builds; a route closed with nobody that lists callers or is switched on by a setting, and a role granting nobody, are refused.
- A through naming a permission the role does not grant, a client not declared or an empty list, or written where no token carries the application the caller signed in through, is refused as through in both builds.
- specarch derive writes refused for every caller for a closed route, refused for a signed-in person where people is absent, refused for every caller not listed, refused with a bad signature from each client that signs, refused through a client not listed for each role whose through narrows the permission, the version case for each client with an admitted range, and refused for a service's own token at every route for people once a service exists.
- The technical specification's matrix has a column per client with roles, a cell that names the clients a grant holds through, a table of the clients with their kind, admitted versions, roles and proof, and a table of the callers of each route.

**Insight:** An identity service served routes open only to named machine clients, routes that also required a signed request, and a route closed to everyone, and each had to be written as a permission with prose, which lost the default-deny caller list and the signature, and a closed route needed a placeholder role, since a permission no role grants is a fail-closed error.

### SA-84

A specification shall be able to declare the token formats its service issues and accepts, each with its kind, lifetime, signature algorithm, claims and checks, one of them the default, and on an operation the token it accepts and the immediate callers of a transaction token; to fix the audience of every accepted access token; and to say where the security event every refusal of a caller writes goes; specarch validate shall check each in both builds, the derived cases shall cover the expired token, each check, the actor as subject, the audience, the chain and the confused deputy's token forms, each naming its security event, generate openapi shall write the schemes the tokens give, and the technical specification shall show the tokens, the chain and the events.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1, NEED-2, NEED-3.

Acceptance criteria:

- The signature none, an unregistered algorithm, a JWT with no signature, an opaque token with one, two defaults or none, an operation naming an undeclared token, a check over an undeclared claim and a claim typed unlike the caller property of its name are each refused in both builds, with the same words.
- A registered claim retyped and an underscore claim outside the registry are refused as claim; a transaction token that is not a JWT, lacks a required claim, writes aud, or is accepted where through reaches without tctx.application is refused as token; via missing, present where not needed, empty, naming an undeclared client, an application, a repeat or a service without a workload-identity proof is refused as via; an accepted access token without a fixed audience or with an audience that is not a URI is refused as token_audience; tokens with clients and no securityEvents, or a store or alarm that is no dependency, are refused as security_events.
- A valid tree with two tokens derives denied with expired <token> on each operation that accepts one, each check as a case, refused when the actor is the subject, refused with a token for another audience, refused with a caller not listed in via, and the confused deputy's token forms once a service exists, each ending with its security event and severity once securityEvents is declared.
- generate openapi writes a bearer scheme named after each accepted access token, with bearerFormat JWT for a JWT, an apiKey scheme in the Txn-Token header for a transaction token, and each operation's security requirement naming the token it accepts.
- The technical specification lists the tokens with their kind, header, audience, lifetime, signature, claims and the operations that accept them with their via, draws the chain via gives, and lists the security events with their severities, the store and the alarm channel.

**Insight:** An identity service issues access, refresh, step-up, delegated and machine tokens, each with its own claims and lifetime, and the claims were only in prose, so a requirement such as the actor claim never equals the subject could not be checked against the binding, a token minted for one service could be replayed at the next, and a refusal left no event behind.

### SA-88

An estate shall be able to keep its clients, roles and trust domain in one identity module that every other module names by reference, and specarch validate shall resolve those references when the modules are given together, count them as unresolved when they are not, and check what the referenced clients and roles allow at every hop.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2, NEED-3.

Acceptance criteria:

- trustDomain, written in the identity module's root file, is a URI, or is refused as token_audience in both builds.
- A role may grant <dependency>#/permissions/<name> and narrow it by through; via and callers may name <dependency>#/clients/<name>; a test's caller may be <dependency>#/roles/<name>. Each is resolved when the specification it names is given in the run, and a name that specification does not hold, or a reference to the wrong kind of element, is refused as reference at the entry, the same in both builds.
- A module with a dependency of kind identityProvider counts each permission no role of its own grants as an unresolved reference while the identity module is not given, and specarch gaps lists it; given, a permission no role of either grants is refused as permission_ungranted.
- When the modules are given together, the chain is found by induction through calls, a client named in via being the module whose info.name is its name; a module named in via none of whose operations calls the operation, a calling operation that accepts no token, and a module that calls the operation and is not in its via are each refused as via at the operation; and two modules of an estate accepting one aud value on access tokens are refused as token_audience at the estate.
- A transaction token accepted where a service exists derives refused with a scope no edge of its chain checked, a confused-deputy case with its security event, in both builds.
- document techspec, given the modules together, writes the identity module's matrix of every module's permissions by its roles and its clients with roles, the cell naming the clients a through narrows a grant to, with the trust domain; gives each other module's matrix a column per role and client of the identity module that reaches its permissions; and draws the chains the induction found, from the person at the edge, with the token and the workload identity on each arrow.
- Once the identity module is given, a client it holds is checked in via and callers as a client of the module is, so an application or a service without a workload-identity proof in via, a service with no roles or a client none of whose roles grants the operation's permission in callers; and a service with no roles is not reported unused when another module names it in via.

**Insight:** The clients, the roles and the trust domain are facts of the whole estate, not of one service, and every hop of a call must check the same names; kept in each module they drift apart, and kept in the umbrella they would put design into a file that only lists and pins the modules (ADR-107).

### SA-89

specarch extract go, swift, javascript and dart shall read the project's own checks of the clients, the application, the immediate caller and the audience, and its event writers, as the implementation file names them, write the clients and the services its checks name as literals as an operation's callers and via, and ask for everything else the code reads at run time; extract go shall also ask for the transaction token of an operation whose handler reads the Txn-Token header.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- The implementation schema's http binding takes clientChecks with an optional clientArgument, and applicationChecks, callerChecks and audienceChecks each with the argument that carries the names, and eventWriters.
- A client check whose argument gives the clients as literals writes them as the callers of each operation it guards, and a caller check the services as its via, each with one must question per check asking for their declaration, which holds the errors of the names not declared yet; given otherwise, such as from a setting, each is a must question naming where the code reads them. Strings a check's call passes after the argument that names are a must question and written nowhere, and two or more literal checks of one kind on a route give the names every one lists, with a must question where their lists differ.
- An application check is a must question for the through of every role that grants the operations' permission, naming any operation that checks the same permission without it; an audience check is a must question at the tokens with its literal or the setting it reads; an event writer is named and nothing is written from it.
- An operation whose handler reads the Txn-Token header gets a must question for its transaction token and its via.
- extract swift, javascript and dart find each check where they find a permission check, and write and ask the same as extract go.
- specarch extract permissions reads a grant's client, the row's subject when it is a client, as a role named after it held by the client declared as a service, with a must question for its proof and a could question to rename the role, named with -client added where a role of the table has the client's name, with a must question whether the client holds that role; and a grant's through as the role's through, the client declared as an application; a grant both narrowed and not by two rows, and a name used as subject and as through, are must questions, and so are what each client is and which token carries the application.

**Insight:** An estate written from its code has its application, caller and audience checks in middleware the project writes its own way; read as nothing, the operations look open to any caller, and guessed, a condition on a grant could be written where none holds (ADR-106, ADR-109, ADR-111).

### SA-91

A specification shall be able to say a tenant scope once, as tenant with the caller's property, the key every tenant-owned entity carries and the entities every tenant reads whole; the document as read shall hold the rows rule of every role over every entity that carries the key, except where the role writes its own, and specarch validate shall refuse in both builds an entity that no rule limits and that the scope does not name as shared.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1, NEED-2, NEED-3.

Acceptance criteria:

- For every role and every entity with a field named key that shared does not list, the document as read, which model prints, holds the rule `<key> == caller.<property>` under the role's rows at the position of tenant, and a rule the role writes for that entity stands in its place.
- An entity that carries no field named key, is not listed under shared and is not limited by a rule of its own on every role is reported as tenant at the entity, in both builds, with the same words; so are a shared name that is no entity, a shared entity that carries the key, a property the caller does not declare, and a key the entity cannot compare with the property; a scope in a specification with no roles is reported as tenant at tenant, since no rule is derived.
- The derived cases of the derived rules, the drafts specarch derive writes for them, the rows the technical specification shows for each role and the row security policies generate sql writes are the ones of the same rules written by hand.

**Insight:** In a multi-tenant suite every role's rule over every tenant-owned entity is the same expression, written by hand hundreds of times, and an entity whose rules are forgotten is reached whole by every tenant with no word from the validator (ADR-179).

### SA-92

specarch generate ui shall write the content pages of a specification for the web, in plain JavaScript through specarch-gen-ui and on Next.js and Carbon through specarch-gen-ui-typescript, from one reading of their blocks, with every text a string key on Next.js; specarch-gen-ui-swiftui shall refuse them by name and write nothing for them.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- specarch-gen-ui writes each public content page as HTML alone, its blocks in order under the title, a heading at its level, the image with its alternative text, and each link to the page's file or to its address; a content page that needs a permission is refused at its permission, since the files reach anyone with the page's text inside.
- specarch-gen-ui-typescript writes each content page as a schema of its title, permission and blocks, every text a string key in the strings file, and a page.tsx drawing ContentPage with the routes its links open, inside the Guard with the derived refusal test when it needs a permission, warned that its text reaches the browser.
- Both web generators refuse, at the block, an image without its text, a link without its label and a link to a page that does not exist or whose route takes a parameter, and leave the page out.
- specarch-gen-ui-swiftui reports each content page as an error at the page and writes nothing for it.

**Insight:** A website is mostly pages of copy, images and links; without a page kind for them the site is written by hand around the generated forms, and its copy has no place among the strings a translation covers (ADR-181).

### SA-93

A specification shall be able to say how a person signs in at an identity provider, as signIn with OpenID Connect's authorisation code flow and PKCE, its provider, client, callback, identity token and back-channel logout, and navigate to signIn from a task page's answer or an action's then; specarch validate shall check every reference in both builds, derive the callback's refusals, and the UI generators and the technical specification shall write the flow, with the provider's issuer, keys and client_id the deployment's.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- signIn names a provider that is a dependency of kind identityProvider, a client of kind application, a callback that is a GET operation taking code and state as required query parameters and naming the provider under calls, an identity token that is a JWT declaring iss, aud and nonce with no const or enum on iss or aud, and a back-channel logout only service clients may call; anything else is reported as sign_in at its key, in both builds, with the same words.
- A page event navigates to signIn only from a task page's answer or an action's then, with no with and no message, and only when signIn is declared; anywhere else it is sign_in at the event.
- The callback derives six critical red cases, state does not match, nonce replayed, issuer differs, identity token expired, signature invalid and code used twice, each naming its security event and severity once securityEvents is declared, and none of the token cases of an operation a signed-in caller calls; specarch derive writes them as drafts.
- A deployment of a specification with signIn gives signIn.issuerUrl and the client's clientId, and one of a specification without signIn gives no signIn; anything else is sign_in at the deployment.
- specarch-gen-ui writes identity-provider.js and the answer or action that leaves for it; specarch-gen-ui-typescript writes the provider in application.ts from the environment and the answer that leaves for it; specarch-gen-ui-swiftui writes the answer that leaves for it through the system's web authentication session; each sends the browser to the authorisation endpoint the provider's discovery document names, with the state, nonce and PKCE verifier going to the callback in the __Host-sign-in cookie.
- The generated go-dxlib handler of the callback names its body as every operation does, and the technical specification shows the flow as a sequence diagram, the checks with the clause that asks for each, and the six security events.

**Insight:** An information system with single sign-on had no element for the redirect, the callback, the state, the nonce and the identity token's checks, so the flow and its refusals were written by hand, untraced and untested by anything the specification produced (ADR-182).

### SA-94

specarch generate ui shall write, for a custom page, the route, the guard and the menu entry, and import the screen from a file the project writes, named in the generated output, so that a missing screen fails the build or the load and never shows a blank page; generate --check shall compare nothing of the project's file, and the technical specification and the manual shall list the page as the project's own screen.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- specarch-gen-ui-typescript writes app/<route>/page.tsx drawing the default export of ./custom/<page> inside the Guard, with the schema of its title and permission, the route's parameters and the routes of its actions, and the derived refusal test when it needs a permission.
- specarch-gen-ui-swiftui writes <Page>View drawing <Page>Screen, a view the app declares, inside the Guard, with the schema, the route's parameters and the routes of its actions.
- specarch-gen-ui writes <page>.html, which says which module did not load until it shows, and <page>.js, which imports custom/<page>.js and calls its show; pages.js names that module, and a custom page that needs a permission is warned of at its permission, since these files have no route guard.
- generate --check passes with the project's file in the output folder and compares nothing of it.
- The technical specification lists a custom page as the project's own screen with its description, and the manual says it is built by hand, what it is for and where its actions lead.

**Insight:** An editor or a live view is built by hand, and without a page kind for it the screen had no route, guard, menu entry, flow or derived test in the design (ADR-183).

### SA-7

specarch document and specarch generate shall write only into the folder the target owns, and with --check shall fail when the committed output differs.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-3.

Acceptance criteria:

- A run writes the target's files into its folder and nothing elsewhere.
- A run with --check on output edited by hand names the file and exits 1, writing nothing.

### SA-8

Every generated file shall name its source specification, version and meta-model, and a hand-written Markdown document shall change only between its markers.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-3.

Acceptance criteria:

- The first line of a generated document names the root file, its version and the meta-model.
- A marked region is rewritten and every other line of the document is unchanged.

### SA-26

specarch document shall write the change and defect register and the release notes from the records beside a specification, kept current with --check like the other documents.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-3, NEED-5.

Acceptance criteria:

- The register lists open change requests and defects before the closed ones, each with its status, what it affects and its decision.
- The release notes list the releases newest first, each with its changes and fixes grouped as added, changed, removed and fixed.

**Insight:** Reviewers and operators read what changed and why in documents; kept apart from the specification, the history stays out of it and still reaches them.

### SA-14

A code target that specarch does not build in shall be produced by the plug-in specarch-gen-<target> found on PATH, which receives the validated specification on its standard input and answers with the files to write, so that specarch writes them, checks them and keeps them inside the target's folder.

Kind: interface; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-7.

Acceptance criteria:

- specarch generate <target> with no built-in generator and no plug-in on PATH says so and exits 2.
- A plug-in's answer that names a path outside the output folder is refused and nothing is written.

**Note:** From Protocol buffers compiler plug-in protocol, plugin.proto, 2024: A plug-in reads a CodeGeneratorRequest from standard input and writes a CodeGeneratorResponse to standard output; protoc writes the files, so a plug-in never touches the disk. <https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/src/google/protobuf/compiler/plugin.proto>

### SA-15

Every document specarch writes shall show an element's why as an Insight and each of its citations as a Note, next to the element, and shall end with the sources its Notes cite.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-6.

Acceptance criteria:

- An element with a why gets one paragraph labelled Insight, and each citation one paragraph labelled Note that names the source's title, edition, the clause and what it says.
- An element shown as a row of a table gets its Insight and Notes after the table, labelled with the row's name.
- A document whose Notes cite sources ends with a table of exactly those sources.

**Insight:** A reader can skip every Insight and Note and still read the document, or read only them to follow the reasoning; a label on each makes both possible.

### SA-16

specarch document shall write, besides the technical specification, the requirements specification, the test plan, the traceability matrix, the deployment guide and the commissioning procedure with its sign-off sheet.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-3, NEED-5.

Acceptance criteria:

- Each of the five targets writes <target>.md into the folder it owns, with the generated-from header.
- The commissioning procedure has a Result column for every step and a sign-off sheet with a row for every signer.

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3, Software and systems engineering, Software testing, Part 3, Test documentation, 2021, clause 7.2 and 8.3: A test plan and test case specifications are the test documentation items of a project. <https://www.iso.org/standard/79429.html>

### SA-46

An implementation file shall mark an element another stakeholder owns, one mapping at a time, naming that stakeholder; no generator shall write a marked element, and validate, diff, gaps and the gates shall still read it.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2, NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- An entity whose mapping names a stakeholder under ownedBy gets no table from generate sql and no schema from generate openapi, while a foreign key or a reference to it is still written.
- An operation whose mapping names a stakeholder under ownedBy gets no operation from generate openapi.
- A page, or a menu or a menu entry, whose mapping names a stakeholder under ownedBy gets no page and no menu entry from generate ui; a mapping may name a menu or an entry of one, '#/menus/<menu>/items/<entry>', as it names any other element, and one that points at nothing is refused, the same in both builds.
- validate and gaps read the marked element as before, and a question that blocks it still holds generation up.
- ownedBy naming no stakeholder of the specification is reported, the same in both builds.

**Insight:** A system read from its sources often holds parts another team builds and changes, such as a shared table or a service behind the same gateway; the specification must describe them, since the project's code depends on them and its sources cite them, but a project that generated them would overwrite the other team's work or fight it on every change.

### SA-58

specarch generate bpmn shall write, through a plug-in, each workflow of a specification as a BPMN 2.0 XML file with its diagram, and the diagram as SVG, that specarch extract workflows reads back to the same workflow, each problem marked at the element it concerns and a draft labelled as one.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-3, NEED-10.

Acceptance criteria:

- Each workflow is one process in a file of its own, in the sequential subset of ADR-054, with BPMN DI shapes and edges laid out by a fixed rule, so two runs write the same bytes.
- extract workflows reads a generated file back to the workflow's description, step names and kinds, approvers, deadlines, and refusal or escalation, and names its trigger and operations in the questions that merge fills; an approval that is the last step comes back as one.
- Each warning and open question at an element a file shows is marked as an XML comment before that element, in the BPMN file and in the SVG; a problem of one workflow is marked only in that workflow's files.
- Output generated with --unapproved from a specification no approval record covers says it is a draft, in the BPMN file and visibly in the SVG.

**Insight:** A workflow is reviewed by people who read BPMN diagrams and run BPMN engines, so the design must reach them in that format; written by hand, the diagram drifts from the workflow on the first change, and one that cannot be read back cannot take a change made in a modeller back into the specification.

### SA-59

specarch generate shall mark every warning and open question at the entry each generated file shows for it, shall write a draft labelled as one in every file when --unapproved lets it past open questions or a missing approval, and shall write the rest of a target's output with an entry the target cannot express marked at that entry and exit 1.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-3, NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- generate --unapproved on a specification with a must question that blocks an entity writes the target's files, each saying it is a draft and naming the question, and the entity's entry carries the question's mark.
- A warning at an operation is marked above its handler in Go, in x-specarch-marks on the operation in OpenAPI, and a warning at an entity above its table in SQL.
- A target that cannot express one entry writes the rest with an error mark at that entry, prints the error and exits 1; SQL writes no migration then, and an approved run over a migration a draft wrote is an error.
- generate without --out passes over a specification that names no output folder for the target with an output_folder warning and writes the others.

**Insight:** The people who answer the questions judge a result faster from the code and screens than from documents, and a compiler that stops at the first gap hides every other one; a draft that says what it is, with each gap at its entry, shows both without letting unapproved code pass for approved.

### SA-60

specarch document html shall write a specification as one HTML page that opens from the disk with no server and makes no request, with an overview first, every element under an anchor named by its pointer, and every problem linked to the entry it marks and marked at that entry.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-3, NEED-10.

Acceptance criteria:

- The page is one index.html with its styles, its script and its diagrams inside it, a Content-Security-Policy that allows no request, and the generated-from header after its doctype; two runs write the same bytes.
- Every element shown has an id equal to its pointer, with what an id or a fragment cannot hold percent-encoded, and no id appears twice.
- Each error, warning and open question is listed in the order of the problems file and links to the deepest element the page shows that holds its pointer, and that element shows a mark linking back; an element an open question blocks says so and links to the question.
- Entities are drawn as an SVG diagram with their fields and relations, each workflow as specarch generate bpmn draws it, and each page that specarch generate ui writes as its screen without scripts; a page with no screen says why.
- An invalid specification is written all the same, from what could be read, with its errors marked.

**Insight:** Reviewers and testers read a specification long before it is finished and seldom read YAML; one page they can open anywhere, search, and link into by an element's id lets them name exactly what a remark is about, which is what takes it back into the specification.

### SA-61

specarch generate --check shall compare a folder of pages built by hand with what the target writes, saying for each file whether it matches and, for a page's data, which values differ.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- A file the plug-in marks as an object literal is read on both sides in the subset of TypeScript that is also JSON5 and compared by value, so formatting, comments, quotes and trailing commas do not count; each differing value is named by its path, with the value on disk and the one generated.
- A file on disk outside the subset is reported as not comparable, with the line and what was found, and never as matching.
- A file built by hand, which has no generated header, matches when it equals what the target writes without its header, draft notice and problem marks; it says so in a line of its own and is not counted as differing. A generated file is still compared byte for byte.
- The library lending example's sign-in and second-factor schemas, written by hand before the generator, compare equal, and a list schema with one column changed is reported as that column.

**Insight:** Most screens of a project that comes to SpecArch were built by hand; before the generated ones replace them, the owner needs to see, page by page, where the specification and the built screen disagree, without the noise of formatting.

### SA-71

specarch generate sqlc shall write the sqlc queries the design derives against the tables generate sql writes, and leave every other query to be written by hand beside them.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2, NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- An operation that posts an entity is an insert of every column but the ones the database draws and the soft-delete flag, answering the record; a read, a replacement or an amendment by one path parameter, of an entity whose key is one field, reads or changes the record by its key, a softly deleted record left out, an amendment keeping a column the request leaves out.
- An operation with listOf on an entity is a page of it and its total, filtered by each filterable field and each query parameter that names a field, searched case-insensitively over the searchable fields, and sorted by the wire name of each sortable field either way, then by the key.
- A list of a view, a list under a path parameter, a list with a query parameter that names no field held in one column, and a read or change of an entity whose key is not one field are warnings at the operation, and their queries are left to be written by hand; an entity another stakeholder owns gets no query.
- A dialect other than PostgreSQL or MariaDB is an error at the target. A query file in the output folder that the plug-in did not write is never overwritten; generate --check compares it, and it matches when it equals what the target writes but for its header.
- The queries compile under sqlc against the migrations, and the lending desk's query file written by hand differs from the generated one only where the specification and its database disagree.

**Insight:** A project on sqlc writes its queries by hand, and most of them are the same few shapes of every entity; writing those from the design keeps them in step with the tables, and a comparison with the file written by hand shows where the two disagree before the generated one replaces it.

### SA-87

specarch generate scripts shall write, for each guarded operation or command whose change the design says, by a keyword or by the guard's writes, a script that refuses unless the guard's precondition holds on exactly the records it names, makes the change only when told to apply it, checks the exact count of records changed, and changes nothing when it is run again; every other guarded change is left to be written by hand.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- A guarded entry that triggers transitions of the guard's entity with one to state, none of their from states, sets the state field to it, on the record by its key when the operation's path has one parameter, and otherwise on every record in a from state for which the precondition holds; a guarded PUT of the entity by one path parameter sets every column a caller may set; a guarded DELETE by one path parameter deletes the record, or sets its soft-delete flag; any other guarded entry whose guard has writes sets the fields it names, each to the value the operator gives or to a literal, beside a transition it triggers when there is one, or deletes the records, on the record by its key when the path has one parameter, and otherwise on every record for which the precondition holds that does not already hold every value set.
- The script counts the records the change would write, with the key, the from states, the precondition and the soft-delete flag in its condition, and refuses unless the count is recordsChanged; the change carries the same condition, and the script refuses unless it wrote recordsChanged records and a record changed by its key holds what was written.
- A variable the change needs that is not set is refused by name before anything is read, unless its column may be null, when leaving it out sets the column to NULL.
- Without the variable apply set to true, the script runs every check and rolls back, saying how many records would change; a record by its key that already holds what the change writes is reported as already applied and left as it is.
- A guarded POST, a guarded PATCH and a guarded command that triggers no transition, each with no writes, a writes that sets a field stored encrypted, transitions of one trigger with two to states, a transition back to the state it leaves, a keyed change whose recordsChanged is not 1, an entity whose key is not one field, a PUT that sets a field stored encrypted and a PUT that sets no column a caller may set are warnings at the guard, and their scripts are left to be written by hand. A dialect other than PostgreSQL or MariaDB is an error at the target, and a script in the output folder that the plug-in did not write is never overwritten.

**Insight:** A data change typed by hand against a live system is where a wrong condition changes a thousand records instead of one; a script written from the guard checks the state it expects, shows the change before making it and counts what it changed, so the mistake is refused rather than committed.

### SA-90

specarch document shall write the user manual from the flows, menus, pages, roles, problem types and commands, and the operations guide from the endpoints, jobs, channels, dependencies, monitors, procedures, settings and deployments, and a problem type shall say what the person who meets it does next, a command what the person who ran it does after each status it fails with, a monitor what the operator does when its objective is missed, and a job that keeps an item apart who handles a kept item, where it is kept and what they do with it.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-3, NEED-5.

Acceptance criteria:

- specarch document manual writes manual.md with the roles that open a page, each with the pages it opens, a role a job acts as or a client holds left out unless a flow names it as its actor; the menus; each flow's steps as numbered instructions; and each page's purpose, who opens it, its fields or columns, its actions with their confirmation, and per problem it names the message, the condition and the remedy.
- The manual has a section per command with its usage line from the program's name and the command's words, who runs it, its arguments and options, what it reads, writes and prints, and each exit status with what it means and its remedy.
- specarch document operations writes operations.md with the environments and their hosts, a checklist row per monitor, job and dependency, each monitor's response, each job's trigger, role and retries, each channel's carrier, publishers and consumers, each dependency's callers, the endpoints with their permissions, the settings, and the backup, restore and rollback steps.
- The operations guide writes, under the jobs, for each job that keeps an item apart, where a kept item is, the role that handles it and the steps to look at it, try it again or discard it, or one sentence naming deadLetter when the job has none.
- A specification with no pages, flows, commands, monitors or jobs still gets both documents, each empty section one sentence naming the key that fills it, and its errors marked as in every document.
- A problem type without remedy, a command without remedies or a program name, and a monitor without response are read as before, with no error or warning, the same in both builds.
- A job's deadLetter whose role is not a role, or on a job whose retries do not keep an item apart, is refused as job, the same in both builds.
- A command's remedy keyed by status 0, or by a status its exitCodes does not list, is refused as exit_code, the same in both builds.

**Insight:** The people who use a system and the people who run it read a manual and an operations guide, not a technical specification; written by hand both drift from the pages and the procedures, and written from the specification they show early what a page asks of a person, which is where a change request starts.

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207, Systems and software engineering, Software life cycle processes, 2017, clause 6.4.12: The operation process uses the system in its intended environment and supports its users. <https://www.iso.org/standard/63712.html>

### SA-32

SpecArch shall ship versioned idioms that say how each recurring implementation concern is done per stack, apply them to every implementation file by default, let a file exclude or override one with the reason, and check the result, starting with the type rendering of every field on Go and on PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle and MariaDB.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- An idiom key naming no idiom, an exclusion or override without why, an override naming an unknown part or defining one it does not list, rendering a stack that is not the file's, or changing a shipped contract statement is each reported under its rule in both builds; an override copied from an older version is warned about.
- A field that no row of the type rendering matches for a stack of the implementation file, such as a decimal wider than Oracle holds, is reported as idiom_contract.
- An override that replaces the Oracle text rows for MAX_STRING_SIZE = EXTENDED validates without a diagnostic.
- The shipped set holds the fifteen idioms of the first set and ui-components, each statement marked with what checks it, and every one passes the idiom schema and cites only the sources it declares.
- A ui target's framework, given or by its platform's default, is a stack of its implementation file, so specarch idioms lists ui-components for a TypeScript file whose ui target is nextjs-carbon and not for one on plain-javascript, and an override rendering nextjs-carbon in a file on plain-javascript is reported as idiom_stack in both builds.

**Insight:** How a decimal, a text column or a missing value is held on a stack is decided once and read by every generator and every agent; without the table each implementation file restates it in prose, each a little differently.

### SA-11

A specification shall be a folder tree with one root file, specarch.yaml, and one folder per life-cycle stage it keeps, in which a file holds one or a few objects of one kind.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-4.

Acceptance criteria:

- A tree whose root lists its stages and holds each stage's files under that folder validates.
- A file in the wrong folder, a section in the wrong file, a listed stage without a folder, and a folder that is not a stage are each reported as layout.

**Insight:** One file for a whole system grows past what a reader can navigate; a tree whose folder names say what is inside lets the reader walk to a thing.

### SA-12

A specification shall be able to hold every stage of the life cycle, from stakeholders and needs through requirements, design, implementation, tests, deployment, commissioning and operation, each optional until the project reaches it.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-5.

Acceptance criteria:

- A specification with only a requirements stage validates with no error.
- A requirement no design element satisfies, a requirement no test, check or monitor verifies, and a need no requirement refines are reported as warnings once the later stage exists.

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207, Systems and software engineering, Software life cycle processes, 2017, clause 6.4: The technical processes run from business or mission analysis and stakeholder needs definition (6.4.2) through requirements definition (6.4.3), design (6.4.4 and 6.4.5), implementation (6.4.7), verification (6.4.9), transition (6.4.10) and validation (6.4.11). <https://www.iso.org/standard/63712.html>

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, Systems and software engineering, Life cycle processes, Requirements engineering, 2018, clause 6.3 and 6.4: Stakeholder needs are defined first and then transformed into system requirements; each requirement carries attributes and traces to its source. <https://www.iso.org/standard/72089.html>

### SA-23

The validator shall check the records kept beside a specification (change requests, defects, releases, incidents, commissioning runs and approvals) against their schema and against the specification they point into, without the specification pointing back at them.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-5.

Acceptance criteria:

- A record whose file name is not its ID or version, or that sits in another kind's folder, is reported as record_name.
- A record naming a role, requirement, pointer, test, environment or monitor the specification does not have is reported as record_ref, unless the ID falls in a declared change-set or defect-set.
- An implemented change whose additions are not in the specification, a change approved without a decision, a fixed defect without a test that shows the fix, a duplicate of a duplicate, and a commissioning run naming a check that does not exist are each reported under their rule.
- A resolved incident that leads to no defect and no change, and says nothing in noChange, is reported as a warning.

**Insight:** A change, a defect or a release happens once and moves through statuses; kept in the specification it would turn it into a change log, and kept nowhere it could not be checked against what the specification says.

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207, Systems and software engineering, Software life cycle processes, 2017, clause 6.3.5 and 6.4.13: Configuration management records and controls changes to the system and its baselines; maintenance handles the problems and modification requests raised after transition. <https://www.iso.org/standard/63712.html>

### SA-24

The system's version shall be the specification's info.version under Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, and the validator shall check each released version against the release before it and against what it includes.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-5.

Acceptance criteria:

- A released release that includes a change still approved, or a released change whose release does not include it, is reported as release_contents.
- A release that includes a major change but steps only the minor number after 1.0.0, or only the patch number before it, is reported as release_bump.
- An info.version that is not the newest released version, and not a later pre-release whose release is planned, is reported as release_version.
- A requirement's release that is not a release record, or names a withdrawn one, is reported as record_ref, and the test plan groups the requirements by release.

**Insight:** A version number is a promise to everyone who depends on the system; one that steps less than its contents say breaks a client that trusted it.

**Note:** From Semantic Versioning, 2.0.0, clause rules 4, 6 to 9 and 11: A major version zero is for initial development; patch, minor and major versions step for fixes, additions and incompatible changes; a pre-release version is marked with a hyphen; precedence compares major, minor and patch numerically, and a pre-release ranks below its normal version. <https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html>

### SA-25

The toolchain shall compare two versions of a specification, list what was added, changed and removed with the version step each needs, and check the release of the later version against that list.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-5.

Acceptance criteria:

- Two versions that differ in one operation, one entity and one requirement are listed as three lines, each with its impact.
- A release that steps less than the largest change, or that includes no change request or defect naming a changed element, is reported and the command exits 1.
- An invalid specification on either side is compared as far as it can be read, its errors are printed, and the command exits 1.

**Insight:** A release record says what a release carries; only a comparison of the two versions shows whether the specification changed that way.

### SA-13

Every element of a specification, at every stage, may carry a rationale (why) and citations of declared sources (cites), and the validator shall check that every citation names a declared source.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-6.

Acceptance criteria:

- An element with why and cites validates, and a citation of a source that is not declared is reported as source.

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, Systems and software engineering, Life cycle processes, Requirements engineering, 2018, clause 5.2.8: Rationale and source are attributes every requirement should carry. <https://www.iso.org/standard/72089.html>

### SA-73

A specification shall say who runs each environment, the team that builds the system or the customer, and for an environment the customer runs it shall hold a handover, what the customer receives to build, install and run it and what stays whose responsibility, which specarch document shall write for the customer's engineers.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-5.

Acceptance criteria:

- An environment marked runBy customer in a specification with no handover, no release or no rollback is reported as handover at the environment, a handover in a specification with no environment the customer runs is reported as handover, and a handover whose to names no stakeholder is reported as stakeholder, the same in both builds.
- An environment the customer runs with no commissioning check in it, no monitor in it, or no backup and restore procedure is a warning at the environment, held by a must question that blocks the section.
- An implementation's deployment of an environment the customer runs without build, method or infrastructure is reported as handover at the deployment, and a build naming a task the file does not have is reported as build_task.
- specarch document handover writes handover.md with what the customer receives, the responsibilities, each implementation's build with its toolchain, base images and the licences of its dependencies, what the hosts must provide, every setting, the migrations, the release, rollback, backup and restore steps, the monitors, the checks and acceptance tests in that environment and the sign-off sheet, in plain words a reader with no SpecArch knowledge follows; a specification with an output folder for it and no handover is passed over with a warning.
- A specification without runBy, handover, backup, restore, build, method or infrastructure gets the same deployment guide and technical specification as before.

**Insight:** Regulated customers take the source into a repository of their own and build and run production themselves; a deployment guide written for the vendor's hosts says nothing to them, and a handover written by hand drifts from the specification.

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207, Systems and software engineering, Software life cycle processes, 2017, clause 6.4.10: The transition process establishes the capability to provide the service in its operational environment. <https://www.iso.org/standard/63712.html>

### SA-17

A specification shall be able to say what it does not yet know as an open question that names what is asked, who decides, what it blocks and how urgent it is; and the validator shall accept a required key missing exactly where a must question says it is unknown, and nowhere else.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- An entity written as an empty mapping and blocked by a must question validates with no error, and its missing keys are listed under the question by specarch gaps.
- The same entity without the question is reported with the missing keys.
- A question whose blocks names nothing in the specification, whose decider is not a stakeholder, or which sits in another stage's folder, is reported.
- An accepted decision that answers a question still present is reported.

**Insight:** A placeholder looks like data and every tool downstream treats it as data; a question says in the specification itself that something is not known, so nothing can be built on it unseen.

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, Systems and software engineering, Life cycle processes, Requirements engineering, 2018, clause 5.2.6: A complete set of requirements holds no to-be-defined, to-be-specified or to-be-resolved clause; resolving them is iterative, within a time set by risk and dependency. <https://www.iso.org/standard/72089.html>

**Note:** From IEEE Std 830-1998, IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications, 1998, clause 4.3.3: A to-be-determined item is accompanied by why it is open, what must be done to close it, who is responsible and by when.

### SA-18

Every element of a specification may say how it is known, stated, inferred or decided, and the validator shall check that a stated element cites a source, an inferred one says why, and a decided one names an accepted decision.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- An element with origin stated and no citation, one with origin inferred and no why, and one with origin decided naming no decision or a proposed one, are each reported.
- When the root file says the specification tracks origin, every element of a section without one is reported as a warning.

### SA-19

specarch gaps shall list the open questions by stage with what each blocks and who decides, and shall say for every document and code target whether it is ready, a draft or waiting; the same text shall be the document target questions, and every other document shall mark the open questions about its elements.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8, NEED-3.

Acceptance criteria:

- A specification with two must questions in two stages prints them under their stages, lists the missing keys of a blocked element, and exits 1.
- A specification without open questions prints that it has none and exits 0.
- A requirements document whose requirement a question blocks starts with a Draft notice and shows the question under the requirement.

### SA-20

specarch generate shall refuse to run a target while a must or should question blocks a section it reads, and shall refuse without a record that a stakeholder read the current documents and approved the specification's files as they are, unless --unapproved is given; specarch approve shall write that record only when the documents on disk are current.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- generate on a specification with an approval record whose digest matches writes its files; after one byte of one file changes it refuses, and runs with --unapproved.
- approve refuses while a configured document differs from what the specification generates, and writes records/approvals/<version>.yaml once the documents are current.

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, Systems and software engineering, Life cycle processes, Requirements engineering, 2018, clause 6.3.3.6: Requirements validation is subject to approval by the project authority and the key stakeholders. <https://www.iso.org/standard/72089.html>

### SA-30

A specification built from existing documents and existing code shall cite each element to the document section or the code file and line it came from, mappings of an implementation file included, and specarch gaps shall show for every source that lists its outline which elements each section or file produced and which produced nothing.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- A mapping stated without a citation is reported as origin_citation, and one inferred without a reason as origin_reason, in both builds.
- gaps on a specification whose manual and code list their clauses prints, per source, the elements under each clause, the count of clauses that produced nothing, and every citation that names a clause outside the outline.

**Insight:** The owner of an existing system reads a partial specification to find out what the documents and the code really say and where they part; a section of either that produced nothing is the first thing to look at, and it cannot be seen without the outline.

### SA-44

specarch extract shall read one surface of an existing system into a specification tree in which every element carries its origin and cites where it was read, name the commit it read, refuse a source no commit names, and give byte-identical output for the same sources at the same commit.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- extract database on a committed catalogue dump writes a tree that validate accepts with no errors, and a second run writes the same bytes.
- A column type the meta-model cannot hold is printed as a line naming it, and is a could question in the tree citing its table.
- extract database reads a partition as the table it is a partition of, with one entity for the table and none for a partition, one could question at the entity listing the partitions with their bounds, and one for each constraint, index or column setting a partition has of its own, citing the partition's entry.
- A dump older than the last change to the path it was made from, a path with changes not committed and a shallow clone are each refused with status 1.
- extract outline on a folder writes a source listing its files as clauses, and gaps on that tree lists each of them as producing nothing.
- extract router on a committed route table writes one operation per method and path pair, with its path parameters and the permission it checks, that validate accepts with no errors, and a route that checks no permission is a must question.
- extract openapi on a document in dxlib's dialect writes the one privilege an operation's x-dxlib-privileges names as its permission and declares it, maps a name in dxlib_module's capitals by the rule of ADR-076 and declares that permission inferred, and asks a must question for an operation that names none, more than one, public, two names that give one permission or a name the rule cannot map.
- extract go on a committed Go module on dxlib writes each endpoint NewEndPoint registers with literal values as an operation citing its registration's and its handler's file and line, with the parameters the handler reads and the problems it answers, in a code source with reading parsed, and asks a must question for a registration in a loop, behind a condition or computed, and for a parameter read the endpoint does not declare.
- extract go on a committed Go module on dxlib and dxlib_module also writes each table NewModelDBTable declares with literal names as the entity extract database writes for it, the roles its seeds grant with the permissions mapped by the rule of ADR-076, and each setting it reads or a dxlib configuration file holds under configuration, and asks a must question for each gate on a setting it finds in an endpoint's middleware, in the words extract permissions uses.
- extract permissions maps a privilege in dxlib_module's capitals by the rule of ADR-076 and declares the permission inferred, and asks a must question on a grant of EVERYTHING, a name the rule cannot map and two names that give one permission.
- extract workflows on a committed BPMN 2.0 file writes one workflow per process with its approvals, deadlines and operation steps, that validate accepts with no errors, prints a line with the file's line for each element outside the sequential subset and writes it as a could question citing that line, and asks for the operations the file names with a must question that names them.

**Insight:** Reading a large system by hand misses the element nobody happened to look at, and a citation without the commit it was read at goes stale while still looking precise; extraction is rerun to see what changed, so any difference that is not a change in the sources hides the one that is.

### SA-45

specarch merge shall merge the partial specification trees the readers write into one specification that keeps the citations of every tree, turn every disagreement between the trees into a must question that cites both, and give byte-identical output for the same trees in the same order.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- The database and router trees of one repository, read at different commits, merge into one specification with one code source at the newer commit, which validate accepts with no errors and gaps reads, and a second run writes the same bytes.
- Two trees that give the same key of the same element different values merge into the element without that key and a must question citing both.
- Two trees that grant one role different permissions, neither declaring a permission the other grants the role, merge into the role with every grant of both and both trees' citations and no question on the grants; a permission one tree grants that another declares and does not grant the role is left out with a must question naming it.
- A request body one tree gives as a reference to a named schema and another as a shape written in place merges into the reference when the shapes agree in all both say, into the element without the schema and a must question naming the difference when a key both give differs, and into the reference with a should question when only the properties listed differ; the merged specification validates with no error in either order.
- A schema one tree gives and an entity another gives under one name merge into both entries and a must question blocking the schema, citing both, that asks whether they are one element or two; the merged specification validates with no error.
- An element only the code has, merged with a documents tree that speaks of its section, is written inferred, starting its why with "Undocumented, from code.", with a question that is must for an operation, a permission, a role, a personal or credential field, or a source given outside, and should otherwise.
- A tree validate reports an error in, and a source two trees declare differently, are each refused with status 1.
- A question that names the operation a workflow's trigger refers to is left out as joined, and the trigger written, when another tree declares that operation; a name no tree declares keeps its question.
- A printed tree and a parsed tree of one repository merge into operations with both trees' citations; the parsed tree's question whether the running system registers an operation is left out where the printed tree has it, an operation only the parsed tree declares is a must question citing its line, and one only the printed tree has a could question.
- The same rows compare entities with a catalogue tree and roles with a permission table tree; a role both give grants what the permission table grants, a grant only a seed makes is a must question and one only the table holds a could question, and a gate on one check that both trees ask is asked once with both citations.

**Insight:** The comparison between surfaces, and between the documents and the code, is where a specification extracted from an existing system finds what is wrong with it; done by hand it is skipped where the two look alike, and a choice made quietly between two sources hides the disagreement the owner must settle.

### SA-57

Every output SpecArch generates shall name the element of the specification it came from, and a remark made at the user acceptance test shall be recorded as a change request or a defect that names the build it is about, where it was seen, what was observed and what was expected, and why the result was not what was wanted, and shall enter the specification as a decision, a question or a rejection, with what it reaches listed before anything changes.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: proposed; verified by test; refines NEED-10.

Acceptance criteria:

- A web page generated from a page of the specification carries the page's pointer and the pointer of each field and action it draws, and a build for an environment that shows the trace shows the pointer, the version and the digest on screen.
- A change request in the acceptance phase without the build, what was observed or what was expected is reported, and so is one analysed without a cause.
- A decision that answers a change request whose decision is not approved is reported.
- The changes document lists, under each open change request, the tests, outputs, documents and approval its pointers reach.

**Problem:** warning: requirement_unverified: no test, commissioning check or monitor verifies requirement SA-57; add verifies: [SA-57] to the test that shows it is met [requirement_unverified@requirements/requirements/refinement.yaml#/requirements/SA-57]

**Insight:** People never write a complete specification, and the people who will use a system see it first at the user acceptance test; a remark that cannot name the element it is about, or that has no way back into the specification, is lost or applied by hand where the next generation overwrites it.

### SA-64

specarch extract documents shall read a document in any language whose words a vocabulary gives, the English one SpecArch ships or a project's file, write the language on the source, and give for it the elements it gives for the same document in English; specarch merge shall read a number of days in a requirement by the vocabulary of its source's language.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- extract documents with --vocabulary on a document written in a second language gives the counts, the requirements' priorities, the entities' types, required fields and sensitivities, and the questions the same document in English gives, and writes language on the source.
- extract documents with no vocabulary named reads the document by the English vocabulary and writes the tree it wrote before vocabularies were data, byte for byte.
- A vocabulary that lists one word in two lists of one group, such as two sensitivities, is refused with the file, the line and the two lists; a language tag SpecArch ships no vocabulary for, given with no file, is refused with the keys a vocabulary holds.
- A leading table column headed with the vocabulary's row-number word is skipped in every table, and --given-outside writes givenOutside on the source.
- merge reads a requirement's number of days in the units and number words of its source's language, from the shipped vocabulary or the one given with --vocabulary, and says once per source that its requirements are not compared when there is neither.

**Insight:** A document in another language gave its outline and nothing else, every table a could line, since the commitment words, the headers and the units were English in the code; a wrong or missing word has to be one line in a data file that the project changes without a release.

### SA-72

specarch check shall compare a specification with the route tables, permission tables and catalogue dumps of its code, read by the readers of specarch extract, print every difference as a problem at its entry, and exit 1 on a difference the allowlist does not name or a line of the allowlist that names none.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1, NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- An operation the router does not serve, a route the specification does not name and a permission that differs between them are each an error, at the operation or at the route's line in the dump.
- A grant only one of the specification and the permission table holds, after each side's grants are widened by the permissions they imply, is an error at the role or at the grant's line in the dump.
- A table, a column, a type as PostgreSQL spells it, a nullability, a generated default, a primary key, a foreign key, a unique constraint, a check constraint's name or a listed plain index that differs between the tables generate sql writes and the catalogue is an error; the text of a check and an index the mapping does not list are reports that never fail.
- A partition of the catalogue is never compared and never a table the specification does not hold; a partitioned table's index, which the catalogue prints with ON ONLY, is compared as any plain index.
- Each problem ends with an id that names the rule and what the difference is about, the same wherever the entry is written; a difference whose id the allowlist holds is counted and not printed, and the run exits 0 when every difference is allowed or a report.
- A line of the allowlist that no failing difference matches or that repeats one is an error at that line; with --since, so is a line the allowlist did not hold at that revision.

**Insight:** A specification nobody compares with its code drifts and is then read by nobody; a gate that fails on every old difference is switched off, and one whose allowlist may grow lets the drift back in.

### SA-76

specarch extract gateway shall read a gateway table the project's printer wrote from what the gateway loads into a gateway with its forwards, dependencies and settings, asking for what the table does not say; and specarch check shall compare a specification's gateways with it.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: proposed; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- extract gateway on a table with two rows writes the gateway with its claim and two forwards, two dependencies of kind system with their protocol from the addresses, two settings, and must questions for the gateway's description and token and for each dependency's description and timeout, byte-identical twice; a table with a repeated value or a key the format lacks is refused with the reason; with --implementation-out and an environment it writes that deployment's servers with name, url and dependency.
- check reports a forward only the specification holds as forward_not_served, one only the table holds as forward_not_specified, one the table sends to another dependency as forward_differs and a claim that differs as claim_differs, each an error the allowlist may name, forward_differs a report when the row names no service.
- merge leaves the fallback question of SA-79 out when a gateway table's tree answers it, one gateway to one question over the whole merge, every tree's fallback handler's question before any tree's catch-all route's, each pass over the trees in the order given, and keeps a question no gateway is left for open with a line.

**Insight:** The table a gateway forwards by was readable by nothing, and a gateway no check compares with its table drifts as every other part of a specification nobody compares with its code does.

### SA-79

specarch extract go shall read a route whose path is a package-level constant of the module or whose method list is a package-level list no statement of the module changes as it reads a literal one, and shall ask a must question at every fallback handler and catch-all route, in place of silence or a line.

Kind: functional; priority: should; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:
