- extract go writes a route registered with Match on a package-level list of method constants and a path from a package-level constant, in the same package or another of the module, as it writes one with a literal list and path, and asks the must question naming the line for a list assigned, appended to or declared again in a second place, in its own package or in another package of the module through the import.
- extract go asks a must question at a NoRoute, NoMethod, NotFound or MethodNotAllowed registration, at a NotFoundHandler, MethodNotAllowedHandler or HTTPErrorHandler field set on a router a name holds or a struct of the module keeps in a field, at a ServeMux pattern of / with no method given a handler that is no router, at a route whose path ends in a catch-all, a gorilla/mux variable whose pattern can match a slash among them, and at gorilla/mux's PathPrefix given a handler that is no router, each counted as a registration and blocking the design stage until the gateways section exists and gateways after; a fallback in a loop or behind a condition asks the question every registration there asks.

**Insight:** A route registered through the module's own constants was a question where the code was plain, and a handler that takes every unmatched request was dropped with no question, which is the one thing a reader may never do.

### SA-85

specarch decide shall answer an open question in one step, writing an accepted decision record under the next ID that names the question under answers and the stakeholder under decidedBy, taking the question out of its file with the author's other lines left as they were, and printing the entries the question blocked with the keys missing there; and problems.sarif shall carry for every open question, as properties of its result and of the run, what an agent queue needs to put the question to the person who decides and to feed the answer back without reading any other file.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- decide on a must question that blocks two keys of a requirement writes design/decisions/ADR-002.yaml beside ADR-001 with the question as title, the answer as decision, the question's ID under answers and the stakeholder under decidedBy, leaves the requirements file without the question and with every other line unchanged, prints the requirement's file and line with the pointer of each key, and exits 0.
- decide on a question that is the only one of its file removes the questions key with it, and removes the file when nothing but comments is left.
- decide is refused, with nothing written, for a question ID the specification does not hold, naming the open ones; for a stakeholder it does not declare; for a source the root file does not declare; and, when the specification tracks origin, without --source.
- A question's result in problems.sarif carries the question's text and its Insight beside its priority, kind, decider, options and blocked entries, and the run names the specification's folder relative to the log, so that a dispatcher runs specarch decide from the log alone.

**Insight:** Writing the decision and removing the question by hand is two edits in two files under a number that must be the next one, which an agent got wrong often enough; and a dispatcher that must parse the question out of a message, or open the specification to find its folder, is one that reads the text instead.

**Note:** From IEEE Std 830-1998, IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications, 1998, clause 4.3.3: A to-be-determined item is accompanied by why it is open, what must be done to close it, who is responsible and by when.

### SA-86

specarch document comparison shall write the old documents against the refined specification, derived from the elements' origin, their citations and the decisions and from no other input - the stated elements kept from each source by clause, the inferred ones clarified with what they were concluded from, the decided ones added or corrected with their decision and its reason, and the clauses of each source's outline that no element cites - so that a reviewer sees what the refinement changed before approving.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- A specification whose manual lists five clauses, with two stated elements citing it, an inferred requirement, a decided requirement citing nothing, a decided entity citing the manual and a could question citing a clause gets a comparison with the stated elements under the manual by clause, the inferred requirement with its reason, the decided requirement as added and the decided entity as corrected with their decisions, the clause only the question cites as asked about, the clause nothing cites as dropped, and an element without origin listed with its warning.
- A decision's citation of a clause leaves the clause dropped when no element cites it, and a stated element whose citation names no source is listed under Kept with the validator's error at it.
- The comparison is never a draft, is not a row of the outputs table and is not among the documents an approval is of.

**Insight:** Before approving, the reviewer wants to see what the refinement changed against what the old documents said, and whether anything of them was left behind; read by hand from the citations that is slow and skipped where the two look alike.

**Note:** From ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, Systems and software engineering, Life cycle processes, Requirements engineering, 2018, clause 6.3.3.6: Requirements validation is subject to approval by the project authority and the key stakeholders. <https://www.iso.org/standard/72089.html>

### SA-1

specarch validate shall check every specification and implementation file given against the JSON Schema of its kind and meta-model version.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1.

Acceptance criteria:

- A file that breaks the schema is reported with rule schema, its file, line and YAML path.
- A file that passes the schema and every other rule produces no output and status 0.

**Insight:** The schema is the one definition of a file's shape; checking it first means every later rule can assume the shape.

### SA-2

Every reference inside a specification shall resolve to an object of the right kind in the same specification, wherever its file is in the tree.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1, NEED-4.

Acceptance criteria:

- A misspelt relation target, enum, operation, page, algorithm, decision, requirement, need, stakeholder, source or environment is reported with its own rule, naming the file and line of the reference.
- A name defined in two files of the specification is reported with both files.
- An operation, command or page's enabledBy that is not a setting of configuration, or names one that is not boolean, is reported as setting; a valid one derives the case disabled by <setting>, the element refused with the setting off.

### SA-3

Every check constraint, condition of a unique constraint and formula shall parse and type-check in the fixed expression language.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1.

Acceptance criteria:

- An expression outside the subset is refused with a message naming the construct.
- An expression that mixes types without a written conversion is refused with the conversion to write.
- A unique constraint's where is an expression over the entity's fields that gives true or false, like a check; a where on a check constraint is refused.

### SA-4

Every worked example's formula, evaluated on its inputs with exact arithmetic, shall give its expected value.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1.

Acceptance criteria:

- An example whose expected value is off by one cent is reported with the computed value.

### SA-5

Access shall be fail-closed; every permission used is declared, and every declared permission is granted by a role or is public.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1.

Acceptance criteria:

- An operation, command or page without a permission is a schema error.
- A permission no role grants is reported, also when it has no description; only a must question that blocks the permission itself covers it.
- A separation-of-duties set names two or more declared permissions, none of them public, and a cardinality from 2 to the number it names; a role that grants that many of the set is refused (separation_of_duties), and the techspec lists, for each set, the combinations of roles that together reach it, as roles never to be given to one person.

### SA-6

Every problem shall be reported, one line each, with file, line, YAML path and rule; the exit status is 0 when valid, 1 when invalid, 2 on a usage or read error.

Kind: interface; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1.

Acceptance criteria:

- A run on a folder with three problems in two files prints three lines and exits 1.
- A run with no arguments prints how to use the command and exits 2.

**Note:** From The go command, Go documentation, 1.26: The Go tools print one problem per line as file:line, which editors and CI already parse. <https://go.dev/doc/>

### SA-9

A specification and its implementations shall be separate files; a specification holds no stack-specific key and an implementation file adds no design.

Kind: constraint; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- A stack-specific extension key in a specification is reported as stack_key.
- A design keyword in an implementation file is reported as design_key.

### SA-10

An implementation file's implements and pointers shall resolve in the specification it names, at the same version.

Kind: functional; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-2.

Acceptance criteria:

- An implementation written against an older version of its specification is reported as implements.
- A pointer to an object the specification does not have is reported as design_ref.

### SA-51

specarch shall list every problem of a specification, valid or not, in one problems file and its SARIF 2.1.0 form, each error, warning and open question with a stable id, file, line and column, JSON pointer, rule, a message saying how to fix it, and notes at the sources it came from and the entries it blocks, and every file specarch writes shall mark the entry a problem touches.

Kind: interface; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-1, NEED-8.

Acceptance criteria:

- specarch document problems on a specification with an error, a warning and a must question writes problems.txt with one line each in the form file:line:column: severity: pointer: rule: message [id], sorted by file and line, the question followed by a note at each source it cites and each entry it blocks, and exits 1.
- The same run writes problems.sarif, a SARIF 2.1.0 log with the same results, the question as kind open and level none, and each id as a partial fingerprint; a second run writes the same bytes.
- A specification with no problem gets a problems file that says so.
- A fragment with one entry that does not parse reports one yaml_syntax error at that entry's line and pointer, keeps its other entries, and reports no reference to the broken entry's name; an implementation file with a broken entry still names the problems file's folder.

**Insight:** People fix a specification the way they fix code, from a compiler's list of problems, one place at a time; a tool that refuses an invalid specification, or lists errors and questions in different places, hides what the author has to fix.

**Note:** From Static Analysis Results Interchange Format (SARIF) Version 2.1.0, 2020, clause result: A result names its rule, its kind and level, its locations, and partial fingerprints that recognise it in a later run. <https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/sarif-v2.1.0.html>

### SA-74

specarch model shall print, in both builds, one JSON document in RFC 8785's canonical form that holds, for every specification of the folders given, the merged document, every node's file, line and column, every resolved reference with the keyword that made it, the layout problems, and each implementation file and estate, so that a program reads a specification as specarch does without a loader of its own.

Kind: interface; priority: must; status: accepted; verified by test; refines NEED-3, NEED-7.

Acceptance criteria:

- specarch model on a folder with a valid specification prints one JSON document whose positions name, for every entry the problems file could name, the file, line and column the problems file would report, and whose references list every satisfies, verifies, $ref, target, permission, emits, calls, decidedIn and implements link with its from, to and through; the Go build and the Swift build print the same bytes.
- A folder with a layout problem is printed with that problem in the problems file's form and exit status 0; a folder with no specification, or one that cannot be read, is exit status 2 and the reason on standard error.
- The validator's errors, warnings and open questions are not in the document; the problems file is their one list.

**Insight:** An editor or any other program that draws from a specification would otherwise load the files itself, a second loader in another language that drifts from the first; one command in both builds, printing one byte form, gives it what specarch reads and lets the conformance suite hold the two builds to the same document.

## 5. Constraints

| Constraint | Kind | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| CON-1 | technical | Every keyword that a standard already has is taken from that standard with its meaning; SpecArch adds a keyword only where none exists. |
| CON-2 | technical | The program installs with one command and runs in CI without a network. |
| CON-3 | legal | Every dependency is open source under an OSI-approved licence, pinned, and scanned before it is taken. |
| CON-4 | organisational | The repository is public and holds generic material only; no employer's, client's or product's data enters it. |

**Insight on CON-1:** A reader who knows JSON Schema, OpenAPI or AsyncAPI should not learn a second name for the same thing.

**Note on CON-1:** From JSON Schema, a media type for describing JSON documents, 2020-12: Field keywords such as type, properties, required, enum, format and the limits. <https://json-schema.org/specification>

**Note on CON-1:** From OpenAPI Specification, 3.1.0: Endpoint keywords such as paths, parameters, requestBody and responses. <https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0>

## 6. Assumptions

| Assumption | Statement |
|---|---|
| ASSUME-1 | A specification is kept in version control, so its history lives there and in history files, never inside the specification. |
| ASSUME-2 | The people and assistants who write specifications can read YAML and a C-like expression. |

**Insight on ASSUME-1:** Without this the files would need change logs, which the Low IQ Tax principle forbids.

## 7. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| specification | One folder tree rooted at specarch.yaml that describes one system through its life cycle. Its design side, everything but implementation/, is the SpecArch Definition (SDF). |
| implementation file | A file named <name>.<stack>.specarch-implementation.yaml (SIF) that says how one stack builds the specification. |
| stage | One of the six life-cycle parts a specification may keep, each in a folder of its name; requirements, design, implementation, tests, deployment, commissioning. |
| section | One top-level key of the merged specification, such as entities or checks; each belongs to one stage. |
| diagnostic | One problem in one file, printed as one line with the file, the line, the severity, the YAML path, the rule and a sentence. |
| rule | The name of one check the validator makes, as the Rule enum lists them. |
| target | What a document or code command produces, such as techspec or openapi, written into the folder the implementation file names for it. |
| plug-in | An executable named specarch-gen-<target> on PATH that produces a code target specarch does not build in. |
| golden scenario | A test of the path that succeeds. |
| red scenario | A test of a path that is refused. |
